title: A 4,000-line lockfile conflict
summary: Two branches added dependencies and the lockfile conflicts everywhere. Never hand-merge one — regenerate it. Learn the pattern, and the .gitattributes rule that stops the conflict recurring.
mental_model: A lockfile is generated output, not source. Merging two generated files line by line produces something neither tool would ever produce. The correct resolution is always: take one side, then re-run the generator.

write.content:
# generated from requirements.in — do not edit
blinker==1.7.0
click==8.1.7
flask==3.0.0
itsdangerous==2.1.2
jinja2==3.1.3
markupsafe==2.1.5
werkzeug==3.0.1

setup.run: git commit -q -m "Add celery for background jobs"

steps.title: Look at what each branch did
steps.why: Both edited one line of requirements.in and both regenerated the lockfile, which rewrote large parts of it. The source change is tiny; the generated change is not.

steps.title: Merge and get two very different conflicts
steps.why: requirements.in conflicts on one line and is trivially resolvable. requirements.lock conflicts across the file — and no amount of careful reading will produce a correct answer, because the correct answer is whatever the generator would output.
steps.expect: Both files conflicted, the lockfile heavily.

steps.title: Resolve the SOURCE file properly
steps.why: requirements.in is hand-written source and deserves a real resolution: both dependencies belong. Always fix the source first — the generated file follows from it.

verify.label: the source file has both branches' dependencies

steps.title: Do NOT resolve the lockfile by hand
steps.why: Take either side wholesale — it does not matter which, because you are about to overwrite it. `checkout --ours` just gets the conflict markers out of the way.
steps.expect: A valid lockfile with no markers — and the wrong contents, which is fine.

steps.title: Regenerate it from the resolved source
steps.why: The generator is the only thing that can produce a correct lockfile. This one command is the entire correct resolution, and it is the same in every ecosystem: `npm install`, `pip-compile`, `bundle lock`, `cargo update`.
steps.expect: A lockfile containing flask, redis AND celery — which neither branch had.

verify.label: the regenerated lockfile has every dependency
verify.hint: resolve requirements.in, then re-run the generator

steps.title: Commit the merge
steps.why: One merge commit containing a correctly resolved source file and a correctly generated lockfile. Anyone reviewing it sees a coherent result rather than an invented one.

steps.title: Make the next one quieter
steps.why: Marking generated files in `.gitattributes` documents the rule for humans and can hand git a merge driver. Some teams go further and stop tracking lockfiles in libraries — but for applications you want the lockfile committed, so this is the pragmatic middle.

write.content:
# Generated: never hand-merge. Take one side and re-run ./regenerate.sh
requirements.lock merge=ours linguist-generated=true
package-lock.json merge=ours linguist-generated=true

actions.run: git commit -q -m "Mark lockfiles as generated for merges"

steps.expect: check-attr reports merge: ours for the lockfile.

verify.label: the lockfile has a merge driver so it stops conflicting
the lockfile contains every dependency from both branches
verify.hint: regenerate it — do not merge it line by line

verify.label: the source file was resolved by hand, correctly
a merge driver is configured so the next conflict is automatic

pitfalls: Never resolve a lockfile by hand. The result is a file the package manager would never generate, and it fails at install time on someone else's machine.
`merge=ours` needs a driver defined too (`git config merge.ours.driver true`), and that config is per-clone. Document it in your contributing guide.
Taking 'ours' silently drops the other branch's dependency until you regenerate. The regeneration step is not optional.
Some teams stop committing lockfiles to avoid this. For an application that is a mistake — the lockfile is what makes builds reproducible.
cheatsheet: clear the markers, contents do not matter
the actual resolution: npm install, pip-compile, bundle lock
define the driver the attribute names
